name: Question 1
problem: What is ${\int }_{2}^{4}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x$ expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?
worked_solution:
The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}f({x}_{m})\cdot Δx,
$$

where ${x}_{m}=a+mΔx$ and $Δx=\frac{b-a}{n}.$

In the definite integral

$$
{\int }_{2}^{4}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x,
$$

the function is $f(x)=(x+1)^{2},$ the lower bound is $a=2$ and the upper bound is $b=4.$ So, we have

$$
Δx=\frac{4-2}{n}=\frac{2}{n}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{4}(x+1)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}f({x}_{m})\cdot Δx \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[f(2+m\cdot \frac{2}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[f(2+\frac{2m}{n})\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[{((2+\frac{2m}{n})+1)}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{n}] \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{\sum }_{m=1}^{n}[{(3+\frac{2m}{n})}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{n}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

What is ∫24(x+1)2dx expressed as the limit of a right Riemann sum?

a
 limn→∞∑m=1n[(3+2mn)2⋅2n]
b
limn→∞∑m=1n[(3+mn)2⋅1n]
c
 limn→∞∑m=1n[(4+mn)2⋅1n]
d
limn→∞∑m=1n[(2+2mn)2⋅2n]
e
limn→∞∑m=1n[(2+mn)2⋅1n]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a right Riemann sum as

∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑m=1nf(xm)⋅Δx,

where xm=a+mΔx and Δx=b−an.

In the definite integral

∫24(x+1)2dx,

the function is f(x)=(x+1)2, the lower bound is a=2 and the upper bound is b=4. So, we have

Δx=4−2n=2n.

Therefore, ∫24(x+1)2dx=limn→∞∑m=1nf(xm)⋅Δx=limn→∞∑m=1n[f(2+m⋅2n)⋅2n]=limn→∞∑m=1n[f(2+2mn)⋅2n]=limn→∞∑m=1n[((2+2mn)+1)2⋅2n]=limn→∞∑m=1n[(3+2mn)2⋅2n].
